content.text:
The pattern matches a single phase, the strongly distorted double perovskite Gd2MgIrO6 (mp-1188236).

**Observed peaks.**
- The main peak is at 32.15° (d ≈ 2.78 Å).
- It has side peaks at 30.9° (about 37% of the main peak) and 32.85° (about 20%).
- Smaller peaks sit at 19.05°, 19.85° and 25.1°.
- There are further reflections near 40.6°, 46–47.8°, 52.7° and 58.3°.

**Gd2MgIrO6 (mp-1188236).**
- The cell volume of 242 Å³ for Z = 2 gives a pseudo-cubic perovskite edge of about 3.93 Å. That predicts the main reflection near 32.2°.
- Using an orthogonal sub-cell of about 5.42 × 5.74 × 7.8 Å, the calculated reflections land close to the observed peaks:

| Reflection | d (Å) | 2θ calculated | 2θ observed |
|---|---|---|---|
| (011) | 4.62 | 19.2° | 19.05° |
| (101) | 4.45 | 19.9° | 19.85° |
| (111) | 3.52 | 25.3° | 25.1° |
| (020) | 2.87 | 31.1° | 30.9° |
| (112) | 2.77 | 32.25° | 32.15° |
| (200) | 2.71 | 33.0° | 32.85° |

- The wide 30.9 / 32.15 / 32.85° triplet requires the large a–b difference of this cell.

**Candidates ruled out.**
- **LaSmCr2O6:** its a and b (5.50 and 5.59 Å) are too close. It would give a much tighter split around 32–32.5°, not the observed triplet.
- **Ta2O5:** it predicts a strong peak near 22.9°; the pattern is flat there.
- **Li2RuO3:** it predicts a strong peak near 17.6°, which is absent.
- **CrO2:** its main reflection near 28.3° is absent.
- **SiO2:** its main reflection near 21.9° is absent.
- **CsEr(MoO4)2:** it predicts strong peaks around 27.5–29.5°, which are absent.
- **Ba5Bi3O11:** it predicts a strong peak near 28.4°, which is absent.
- **Mg2Co3O8:** I did not compute its pattern because the triclinic cell is awkward. No unexplained peaks remain to suggest a second phase, which leaves it unsupported rather than excluded.

{"present": ["mp-1188236"], "confidence": 0.8, "note": "The strongly split perovskite triplet at 30.9/32.15/32.85 degrees plus superstructure peaks at 19.05, 19.85 and 25.1 degrees match the distorted Gd2MgIrO6 double perovskite, and no candidate is needed to explain other peaks."}
